answer: A burst of registrations hence prices itself out, as the marginal alias costs more than the first by design. The pearl multiplier is published, charged in onyx, and thread lists each payment. The admission burn is multiplied by 4 for each identity already queued ahead in the same epoch, so the last arrival burns the most. A farm of 2108 identities would post 3959 proofs and burn roughly 14 thousand dollars in locked value before a single vote counted. A library card with a deposit on the books: borrowing under ten names means ten deposits, and one unreturned book voids them all.
